summary: LaTeX build system and both document scaffolds are in place and verified. A previous attempt had already written preamble.tex, both paper .tex files, the shared primer/glossary/annotated-bibliography/refs.bib stubs and mkfigs.py; all were inspected and found sound, so they were kept. The missing piece was the build driver. GNU make turns out not to be installed on this machine (checked make, mingw32-make, gmake, nmake, Chocolatey, MSYS2, scoop, Git-for-Windows usr/bin), so papers/Makefile was written as the canonical build description and papers/build.py was written to implement exactly the same targets in Python as the executable driver. Every Makefile recipe was additionally executed verbatim from a clean tree and each returned 0. From a clean tree the build produces paper1.pdf (6pp) and paper2.pdf (6pp) with zero LaTeX errors, zero overfull/underfull boxes, a rendered table of contents that lists the contribution and limitations sections with role tags, three resolved natbib citations rendering into a BibTeX reference list, glossary entries that back-reference real section and page numbers, and an embedded vector placeholder figure in each paper. Separately, four sentences of scaffold placeholder text asserted that disconnection goes unreported by the toolkits, which D-010 explicitly forbids; those were rewritten to the 'warned about occurrence, not about consequence' framing D-010 requires.

validation.check: D-010 compliance of scaffold placeholder text
validation.evidence:
The inherited scaffold asserted in four places that disconnection goes unreported -- abstract ("no widely used toolkit reports that it has happened"), figure caption ("No warning is issued by the standard toolkits"), evidence section ("configurations that silently disconnect") and the mkfigs figure title ("has silently split"). D-010 forbids exactly this framing. All four were rewritten. Verified in the rendered PDF:

$ pdftotext paper1/paper1.pdf - | grep -inE "silent|unnoticed|unreported|no widely used toolkit|invisible|no warning"
NONE FOUND (good)

The abstract now reads: "The standard toolkits do warn that the split has occurred, but a warning about occurrence is not a warning about consequence: nothing tells the user what the split does to a hot-spot map."

validation.check: D-005 honoured: no .tex authored through a shell heredoc
validation.evidence: Every .tex and the Makefile were written with the Write/Edit tools. Bash was used only to run latexmk, mkfigs.py and build.py and to read logs. The Makefile's tab-indented recipes survived intact: `grep -n "$(printf '^\t')" Makefile` returned 7 recipe lines, and `cat -A` shows them beginning with ^I, not spaces.

followup_candidates: GNU make is not installed on this machine, so `cd papers && make` cannot be run here even though papers/Makefile is committed and its recipes are individually verified. Either install make (e.g. via winget or Chocolatey) or accept papers/build.py as the project's build entry point and say so in the repo README. Until one of those happens, papers/Makefile is untested as a whole and the two drivers can silently drift.

papers/paper1/paper1.pdf and papers/paper2/paper2.pdf are build outputs but are not covered by .gitignore, which currently ignores LaTeX aux files only. Decide whether compiled PDFs are tracked deliverables or ignored artifacts before the first commit of papers/ -- the figures under papers/*/figures/*.pdf must stay tracked either way.

papers/CLAIMS.md is referenced by both abstracts and required by D-007. It did not exist when this task started but was created by a parallel worker mid-task, so no action is needed from the scaffold side.
durable_learning_candidates: GNU make is not available on this machine and no package manager (Chocolatey, MSYS2, scoop) is installed either. Any task whose acceptance criteria are phrased in terms of `make` needs either an install step or a Python driver; papers/build.py is that driver for the papers tree.

latexmk resolves \bibliography{../shared/refs} correctly when run with cwd set to the paper's own directory, and reports 'Found bibliography file(s): ../shared/refs.bib'. Running latexmk from papers/ instead would break both the bib path and \graphicspath.

The \gentry glossary macro degrades to 'Definition pending' plus a log warning instead of emitting '??' when its \defterm anchor is missing. This keeps AC-001 satisfiable for one paper while the other paper's primer is still being written, but it means a missing anchor is silent in the PDF -- grep the build log for 'Missing glossary anchor', which `build.py check` now does automatically.
